QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_41

answer.text: They always give positive real returns
The sovereign can print money to repay obligations in home currency
They are insured by deposit insurance

explanation.text: The Logic: Local-currency government bonds are considered risk-free because the sovereign can print currency to repay. The workbook limits this risk-free status to credit risk only. The Trap: G-Secs can give negative real returns when inflation exceeds the coupon, and their market value can decline with interest-rate rises (price and reinvestment risk). They are not insured by deposit insurance. Note: "Risk-free" in this context refers strictly to credit risk on home-currency sovereign obligations.
